To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
antimony and tin-antimony alloy nanorod electrodes deliver high reversible capacities in alkali ion half cell and full cell configurations.

the use of cetrimonium molecules as surfactant in microwave assisted synthesis of antimony alloy nanoparticles results in self assembled nanorod morphology with a large aspect ratio, which when mixed with nitrogen duced graphene flakes and used as anodes in lithium and sodium ion half and full cells, delivers excellent electrochemical performance.

the formation of antimony and tin-antimony alloy nanorod anodes for lithium ion and sodium-ion secondary batteries can be achieved by a simple microwave-assisted hydrothermal process using the surfactant cetrimonium bromite.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the synthesis and electrochemical performance of Sb alloy nanorods as an anode material for Li+ and Na + full cell applications.
the synthesis of antimony and antimony tin alloy nanorods using a simple microwave hydrothermally assisted strategy and the use of these materials as electrodes for alkali ion full cells.
the synthesis of novel nanostructured antimony alloy based materials for the first time and their practical application in alkali ion full cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the present work provides a facile and scalable microwave hydrothermal approach to fabricate antimony and tin alloy nanorods with high aspect ratios, which are promising anode materials for Li+ and Na+-based alkali ion batteries.

the present study reports a facile microwave assisted hydrothermal synthesis of antimony alloy nanoparticles with an average aspect ratios of 6, which are subsequently used as an anode material in alkali ion full cells.
the present study provides a facile approach to fabricate antimony and tin-antimony alloy nanostructures with improved electrochemical properties.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the use of cetrimonium assisted microwave hydrothermal approach to prepare Sb Sn alloy nanorods can be used to significantly improve the electrochemical performance of Sb based electrodes in both Li+ and Na + secondary batteries.
the unique nanostructuring strategy employed in this study is highly promising for the practical application of antimony alloys in alkali ion batteries.
we have successfully demonstrated the use of antimony alloy anodes with a high energy density and excellent cycling stability for both Li+ and Na + secondary batteries.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of cetrimonium based capping agents can be a simple, yet effective strategy for the synthesis of nanostructured antimony alloys for alkali ion battery applications.
the use of cetrimonium molecules as a soft template is a viable strategy to prepare antimony and antimony tin alloy nanorods with improved electrochemical properties for use in alkali ion full cells.
the antimony alloy nanomaterials can be used as a low cost and sustainable anode for both Li+ and Na + secondary batteries.
